security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel executes CSR read/write to eithreshold or eidelivery on a hart implementing Smidctrl/Ssidctrl but not full IMSIC, where these CSRs are no longer architecturally present per the revised spec, causing either an illegal-instruction trap or (if the access is caught and emulated) undefined interrupt-priority behavior during critical sections such as spinlock-held regions or context-switch windows.
security_spec.summary: Removal of eithreshold/eidelivery from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope breaks FreeBSD's interrupt-threshold gating on ACLIC-only systems, opening critical-section race windows when the kernel expects threshold-based masking but the CSR is absent or repurposed as mithreshold with different (major+minor identity) semantics.

findings.finding: No CSR_EITHRESHOLD or CSR_EIDELIVERY definitions exist anywhere in encoding.h. The CSR number space between 0x106 (SCOUNTEREN) and 0x140 (SSCRATCH) — where eithreshold (0x108) would reside — is left unpopulated. No macro, constant, or register name references these removed CSRs.

All CSR access macros (csr_read, csr_write, csr_swap, csr_set, csr_clear) operate via inline assembly with statically-named CSR operands (e.g., sstatus, sie, sip, satp, stimecmp). No dynamic CSR-number indexing or indirect CSR access mechanism exists that could inadvertently hit eithreshold/eidelivery encodings. The CSR_ZIMM helper only checks for immediate-value optimization, not CSR selection.

Trap handlers only read sstatus (SSTATUS_SPP, SSTATUS_SIE, SSTATUS_SUM) via csr_read. No access to eithreshold or eidelivery CSRs in interrupt/exception entry or exit paths, so context-switch windows cannot trigger undefined interrupt-priority behavior from removed CSRs.
pmap_activate only writes satp CSR. No eithreshold/eidelivery manipulation during address-space switches, consistent with absence of these CSRs.

Interrupt controller enable/disable manipulates sie CSR via csr_set/csr_clear with individual IRQ bits. No eithreshold/eidelivery access — priority-threshold-based interrupt masking is handled through the APLIC memory-mapped IDC_ITHRESHOLD register (MMIO, not CSR).

APLIC driver uses APLIC_IDC_ITHRESHOLD which is a memory-mapped IO register (offset 0x0008 within the APLIC IDC structure), not the eithreshold CSR. This is architecturally correct: on systems with APLIC+IMSIC, interrupt threshold is configured through the APLIC's own MMIO interface, independent of the removed eithreshold CSR. No risk of illegal-instruction trap.

bhyve's virtualized APLIC emulates the IDC_ITHRESHOLD MMIO register (offset 0x8 within IDC structure) in a switch-case handler. This is memory-mapped IO emulation, not CSR access. The virtualized APLIC correctly does not reference eithreshold or eidelivery CSRs.

Root cause analysis: eithreshold, eidelivery, Smidctrl, and Ssidctrl have zero presence in the entire freebsd-src tree. No #define, no CSR access, no feature detection, no emulation fallback. The PR to remove these CSRs from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl is consistent with current code — the code was never using them. The only interrupt-threshold concept in the tree (APLIC_IDC_ITHRESHOLD) operates through MMIO and is architecturally distinct from the removed CSR-based eithreshold.
